researcher: Claude (web research session); every source below was opened and read for the cited facts on the date shown
thesis: Planet Fitness can charge a very low price partly because its clubs are sized for the share of members who actually show up, and the company's own filings point to that share being small.

contradictions.note: Planet Fitness does not state anywhere in the 10-K that its model depends on non-attendance, and the 10-K gives no members-per-club or capacity figure. Resolution: the video presents the capacity logic as OUR arithmetic on disclosed numbers (inferences i1-i3), not as a company statement, and says so on screen and in narration.
'Workouts' in the 10-K is undefined (check-ins vs distinct sessions). Resolution: use only as an approximate floor ('more than 650 million') and say the definition is the company's.
The academic study covers three non-Planet-Fitness health clubs (1997-2000), so it shows a behavioral pattern, not Planet Fitness behavior. Resolution: attributed only as a general finding.

claims.text: At December 31, 2025 Planet Fitness had approximately 20.8 million members and 2,896 clubs (2,604 franchised, 292 corporate-owned); a year earlier, 19.7 million members and 2,722 clubs.
The FY2025 10-K says members completed more than 650 million workouts in the company's clubs.
The 10-K describes its clubs as typically 20,000 square feet.
Classic Card dues start at $15 a month for new members and the PF Black Card at $24.99; the standard annual fee is $49; Black Card penetration was 66.5% at year-end 2025.
Over 90% of both corporate-owned club and franchise revenues were recurring: royalties, monthly dues and annual fees.
In a study of 7,752 members at three health clubs, members on a flat monthly fee of over $70 attended on average 4.3 times a month, paying over $17 per expected visit versus $10 on a 10-visit pass.
The Classic Card cost $10 a month from 1998 until the May 2024 announcement that new members would pay $15.

inferences.text: 20.8 million members across 2,896 clubs is about 7,200 members per club.

650 million workouts over 2025 spread across roughly 2,800 average clubs is about 230,000 workouts per club per year, or roughly 630 a day (workouts are defined by the company and the average-club count is approximate).
650 million workouts across about 20 million average members is about 2.7 workouts per member per month, counting members who never come.
If every member visited at the 4.3-a-month rate in the academic study, a club of 7,200 members would see about 1,000 visits a day, versus about 630 at the 10-K-implied rate.

angle: Not 'gyms are a scam'. A capacity-and-incentives explanation built only from the company's own disclosed numbers, with the limits of the evidence shown on screen.
